title: German Translation, Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Dutch Blended Physiotherapy Checklist
summary:
Digital services are becoming increasingly important in physiotherapy. Since April 2022, exercise programs via apps or therapy sessions via video have been available as part of standard care for statutory health insurance beneficiaries in Germany. The combination of face-to-face treatment in the practice and digital elements is called "Blended Physiotherapy."
However, Germany currently lacks suitable tools to decide which patients would benefit from this combined treatment approach. In the Netherlands, a checklist was developed for this purpose (Dutch Blended Physiotherapy Checklist, DBPC for short). This checklist helps therapists assess whether a patient is suitable for the combination of in-person and video-based treatment and how it can best be designed.
Since this checklist is currently only available in Dutch, the aim of this study is to translate it into German, adapt it to the German healthcare context, and test whether it works reliably and is practical for everyday clinical use.
The study consists of two phases: First, the checklist will be translated by experts and tested for comprehensibility with 30 to 40 therapists. Then, the German version will be completed by approximately 150 therapists together with their patients twice, with an interval of 7 to 21 days between applications. This allows us to verify whether the checklist produces reliable results and whether it can be easily integrated into daily clinical practice.
The results of this study should help therapists make better decisions about which patients can benefit from digital treatment options and how these should be individually designed.
conditions: Diseases of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue
Injury, poisoning and certain other consequences of external causes
Symptoms, signs and abnormal clinical and laboratory findings, not elsewhere classified
Factors influencing health status and contact with health services

interventions.name:
Phase 1 of the study: German translation and cross-cultural adaptation of the DBPC

The DBPC will be translated from Dutch into German and adapted to the German healthcare context following established methodological guidelines for the translation and cross-cultural adaptation of measurement instr

Phase 2 of the study: Psychometric testing of the DBPC

The German version of the DBPC will be applied by physiotherapists and patients in outpatient and day-care physiotherapy settings in Germany and tested for selected quality criteria. The psychometric testing focuses on test-retest reliability

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Physiotherapists:
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Professional license in Germany
- Working in outpatient or day-care settings
- Excellent German language skills (level C1, C2, or native speaker according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages)
- Informed consent to participate in the study

Patients:
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Physically and mentally suitable for telemedicine services according to § 125 Abs. 1 SGB V
- Therapy goal is achievable regardless of treatment format (face-to-face or telemedicine)
- Valid prescription for one of the following services: individual physiotherapy, group physiotherapy, physiotherapy for cystic fibrosis, neurological physiotherapy for adults (Bobath concept), manual therapy
- Informed consent for anonymized data collection
Exclusion criteria:
Physiotherapists:
- Working exclusively in inpatient settings
- German language skills below C1 level

Patients:
- Physical or mental inability to participate in telemedicine services
- No valid prescription for approved services
